n: Whoever makes God their hiding place lives safely in his shade. ‘Most High’ and ‘Almighty’ are two titles stressing God’s supreme power to protect.

f.g: A hidden shelter or hiding place.

n: The psalmist personally confesses his trust: the Lord is his refuge and fortress. The rest of the psalm explains what that trust brings.
God rescues from hidden traps, like a bird-catcher’s net, and from deadly disease. ‘Noisome’ means harmful or destructive.

f.g: A bird-catcher’s trap — a picture of hidden danger.

n: A tender image: God shelters his people as a mother bird covers her young with her wings. His truth is like a large shield and a small shield together.

f.g: A small round shield; here paired with the large shield for full protection.

n: The believer need not fear dangers that come at any hour — night terrors or daytime attacks.
Plague that creeps in darkness and destruction that strikes at noon are named together to cover every time of day.
Even if multitudes fall all around, the one who trusts God will not be overcome. This is poetry about God’s protection, not a guarantee that believers never suffer.
The faithful will simply watch as the wicked receive the results of their own choices.
The reason for this safety: the believer has made the Most High their home.
No disaster will overtake the faithful one’s home. Compare the Passover, when the destroyer passed over Israel’s houses.
God commands his angels to guard his people on every path. Satan later quoted this verse to tempt Jesus.

f.w: give his angels charge over thee

n: Angels carry the faithful as if in their hands, protecting them from stumbling. Jesus refused to test God by misusing this promise.

f.w: dash thy foot against a stone

n: The faithful will overcome fierce dangers, symbolized by lions and snakes. Jesus gave his disciples similar power over serpents.

f.g: Here a serpent or sea creature.

n: Now God himself speaks. He promises to rescue and lift up the one who clings to him in love and knows his name — that is, knows him personally.

f.g: Clung to me in love; held fast to me.

n: God promises to answer, to be present in trouble (not just to remove it), to rescue, and to honor.

f.w: I will be with him in trouble

n: The final promise: a full life and a vision of God’s salvation. For Latter-day Saints, ‘salvation’ ultimately points to eternal life through Jesus Christ.
